payload.translation: The Way that can be spoken is not the Way; the Name that can be named is not the Name; the Nameless is the beginning of Heaven and Earth, the Name has the Mother of all things. The Way without desire sees its wonder; the Way with desire sees its limits. These two are one in origin but different in name. They are both called the "Mysterious" (Xuan). The Mysterious is the Mysterious again and again; the Gate of the Many Mysteries.

issues.span: the Name has the Mother of all things
issues.advice: The source 有名萬物之母 means 'the named is the mother of all things'; 'has the Mother' misrenders the copula and reverses the relation.

issues.span: The Way without desire sees its wonder; the Way with desire sees its limits
issues.advice: The source 常無欲以觀其妙 / 常有欲以觀其徼 lacks an explicit subject 'The Way'; it describes the constant absence/presence of desire as the means of observing wonder and limits, not the Way itself seeing.

issues.span: the Gate of the Many Mysteries
issues.advice: 衆妙之門 is 'the gate of all wonders/marvels'; 'Many Mysteries' shifts 妙 (wonder/marvel) to 'mystery' and is not accurate.

issues.span: The Mysterious is the Mysterious again and again
issues.advice: 玄之又玄 is idiomatically 'mystery upon mystery' or 'the mystery of mysteries'; the literal repetition is awkward in English.

issues.span: the "Mysterious" (Xuan)
issues.advice: Inconsistent handling of 玄: it is glossed as 'Mysterious' here but rendered 'Mysteries' later; keep a single consistent term for 玄/妙.

payload.translation: The Way that can be spoken is not the Way; the Name that can be named is not the Name; the Nameless is the beginning of Heaven and Earth, and the Named is the Mother of all things. The Way without desire observes the wonder; the Way with desire observes the limits. These two are one in origin but different in name. They are both called the "Mysterious" (Xuan). The Mysterious is the Mysterious again and again; the Gate of the Many Mysteries.

issues.span: The Way without desire observes the wonder; the Way with desire observes the limits.
issues.advice: The source's 常無欲/常有欲 refers to the subject (the person) being constantly without/with desire, not 'the Way without desire.' Render as 'Constantly without desire, one observes its wonder; constantly with desire, one observes its limits.'

issues.span: the Gate of the Many Mysteries
issues.advice: 衆妙 means 'all wonders/marvels,' not 'many mysteries'; render as 'the Gate of All Wonders.'

issues.span: These two are one in origin but different in name.
issues.advice: 同出 means 'emerge together from the same source'; 'one in origin' is acceptable but 'emerge together' is closer.

issues.span: the "Mysterious" (Xuan)
issues.advice: 玄 is conventionally rendered 'Mystery' or 'the Dark/Profound'; 'Mysterious' as a noun is awkward. Use 'Mystery' consistently.

issues.span: The Mysterious is the Mysterious again and again; the Gate of the Many Mysteries.
issues.advice: The final clause is a fragment; integrate as 'Mystery upon Mystery—the Gate of All Wonders.'

payload.translation: Constantly without desire, one observes its wonder; constantly with desire, one observes its limits. These two are one in origin but differ in name. They are both called the Mystery. The Mystery is the Mystery again and again; the Gate of All Wonders.

issues.span: Constantly without desire, one observes its wonder
issues.advice: The opening lines 道可道非常道名可名非常名無名天地之始有名萬物之母 are entirely omitted; the translation must include the Dao/name paradox and the nameless/named as origin/mother of all things.

issues.span: The Mystery is the Mystery again and again
issues.advice: 玄之又玄 means 'mystery upon mystery' / 'deeper than mystery'; the rendering is awkward and loses the sense of deepening.

issues.span: limits
issues.advice: 徼 is better rendered as 'manifestations' or 'outward forms/boundaries'; 'limits' is acceptable but 'manifestations' is the standard term in Daodejing translations.

payload.translation: Le savoir est-il un savoir qui n'est pas le même savoir, le nom est-il un nom qui n'est pas le même nom, le nom sans nom est le commencement des choses, le nom des choses est la mère des choses, le vide sans désir permet de voir la sagesse, le désir permet de voir la limite. Ces deux sont originaires et ont des noms différents, ils sont appelés le Sombre. Le Sombre est encore le Sombre, et le Sombre est le commencement des choses.

issues.span: Le savoir est-il un savoir qui n'est pas le même savoir
issues.advice: The source 道可道非常道 concerns the Dao/Way (道), not 'savoir' (knowledge). Render 道 as 'la Voie' or 'le Dao'; the first clause should express 'the Way that can be spoken is not the constant Way'.

issues.span: le nom est-il un nom qui n'est pas le même nom
issues.advice: The source 名可名非常名 means 'the name that can be named is not the constant name'; the translation loses the 'constant/eternal' (常) qualifier and the naming relation.

issues.span: le nom sans nom est le commencement des choses
issues.advice: Source 無名天地之始有名萬物之母: 'the nameless is the beginning of heaven and earth; the named is the mother of the myriad things.' The translation collapses 天地 (heaven and earth) into 'choses' and omits the named/nameless contrast structure.

issues.span: le vide sans désir permet de voir la sagesse
issues.advice: Source 常無欲以觀其妙: 'constantly without desire, one observes its subtlety/wonder (妙)'. 'Sagesse' mistranslates 妙; use 'subtilité' or 'merveille'.

issues.span: le désir permet de voir la limite
issues.advice: Source 常有欲以觀其徼: 'constantly having desire, one observes its manifestations/boundaries (徼)'. The '常' (constant) is dropped and the parallel structure with the previous clause is lost.

issues.span: le Sombre est le commencement des choses
issues.advice: Source 衆妙之門 means 'the gate of all subtleties/wonders' (門 = gate/door), not 'the beginning of things'. Render as 'la porte de toutes les merveilles'.

issues.span: le Sombre
issues.advice: 玄 is conventionally rendered 'le Mystère' or 'l'Obscur' in French Daoist translations; 'le Sombre' is non-standard and loses the mystical connotation.

issues.span: le savoir
issues.advice: 道 is a key term consistently rendered 'la Voie' (or 'le Dao'); translating it as 'savoir' is a terminology error that misrepresents the text.

issues.span: Ces deux sont originaires et ont des noms différents
issues.advice: Source 此兩者同出而異名: 'these two emerge together but have different names.' 'Sont originaires' is not idiomatic French; use 'sortent ensemble' or 'proviennent de la même origine'.

payload.translation: La Voie que l'on peut dire n'est pas la Voie qui est toujours la même, le nom que l'on peut nommer n'est pas le nom qui est toujours le même, le nom sans nom est le commencement des choses, le nom des choses est la mère des choses, le vide sans désir permet de voir la sagesse, le désir permet de voir la limite. Ces deux sont originaires et ont des noms différents, ils sont appelés le Mystère. Le Mystère est encore le Mystère, et le Mystère est le commencement des choses.

issues.span: le nom sans nom est le commencement des choses, le nom des choses est la mère des choses
issues.advice: The source distinguishes 無名 (the nameless) as the beginning of heaven and earth (天地之始) and 有名 (the named) as the mother of the myriad things (萬物之母). The translation collapses 'heaven and earth' into 'choses' and renders 有名 as 'le nom des choses', losing the nameless/named contrast and the cosmological scope.

issues.span: le vide sans désir permet de voir la sagesse
issues.advice: 常無欲以觀其妙 means 'constantly without desire, one observes its subtlety/wonder' (妙 = subtlety, wonder), not 'sagesse' (wisdom). 'Vide' (emptiness) is also an addition not present in the source.

issues.span: le désir permet de voir la limite
issues.advice: 常有欲以觀其徼 means 'constantly having desire, one observes its manifestations/boundaries' (徼 = boundary, manifestation). The parallel 'constantly' (常) is dropped and the sense of 徼 is narrowed; consider 'ses manifestations' or 'ses limites'.

issues.span: Ces deux sont originaires et ont des noms différents
issues.advice: 同出而異名 means 'they emerge together but have different names' (同出 = same origin/emerge together). 'Sont originaires' is unclear and does not convey 'emerge from the same source'.

issues.span: le Mystère est le commencement des choses
issues.advice: 衆妙之門 means 'the gate of all subtleties/wonders' (門 = gate/door), not 'the beginning of things'. This is a mistranslation of the final clause.

issues.span: la Voie qui est toujours la même
issues.advice: 常道 is conventionally rendered 'the constant/eternal Way' (le Tao constant / la Voie éternelle). 'Toujours la même' is a paraphrase that departs from the established term; consider 'la Voie constante'.

issues.span: le Mystère
issues.advice: 玄 is conventionally rendered 'mystère' but the phrase 玄之又玄 (mystery upon mystery / deeper than any mystery) is flattened by repeating 'le Mystère est encore le Mystère'; consider 'mystère sur mystère' or 'obscurité sur obscurité' to preserve the reduplicative structure.

issues.span: le nom que l'on peut nommer n'est pas le nom qui est toujours le même
issues.advice: The long comma-spliced sentence is hard to follow; the parallel structure of the source (道可道/名可名) would read better with clearer punctuation or semicolons separating the parallel clauses.

payload.translation: La Voie que l'on peut dire n'est pas la Voie qui est toujours la même ; le nom que l'on peut nommer n'est pas le nom qui est toujours le même ; le nom sans nom est le commencement des choses, le nom des choses est la mère des choses ; le vide sans désir permet de voir la sagesse, le désir permet de voir les limites. Ces deux sont originaires et ont des noms différents ; ils sont appelés le Mystère. Le Mystère est encore le Mystère, et le Mystère est le commencement des choses.

issues.span: le nom sans nom est le commencement des choses, le nom des choses est la mère des choses
issues.advice: Source says 無名天地之始 (the nameless is the beginning of heaven and earth) and 有名萬物之母 (the named is the mother of ten thousand things). Translation collapses 天地 (heaven and earth) into 'choses' and renders 有名 as 'le nom des choses' rather than 'the named'.

issues.span: le vide sans désir permet de voir la sagesse
issues.advice: Source 常無欲以觀其妙 means 'constantly without desire, one observes its subtlety/wonder' (妙 = subtlety, wonder), not 'la sagesse' (wisdom).

issues.span: le désir permet de voir les limites
issues.advice: Source 常有欲以觀其徼 means 'constantly having desire, one observes its manifestations/boundaries' (徼 = boundary/manifestation); 'les limites' is acceptable but should reflect 常有欲 (constant desire) and parallel structure.

issues.span: Ces deux sont originaires et ont des noms différents
issues.advice: Source 此兩者同出而異名 means 'these two emerge together but have different names' (同出 = emerge from the same source), not merely 'sont originaires'.

issues.span: et le Mystère est le commencement des choses
issues.advice: Source 衆妙之門 means 'the gate of all subtleties/wonders', not 'the beginning of things'. This is a significant mistranslation of the closing phrase.

issues.span: la Voie qui est toujours la même
issues.advice: 常道 is conventionally rendered 'the constant/eternal Way'; 'toujours la même' is a loose paraphrase. Consider 'la Voie constante/éternelle'.

issues.span: le Mystère
issues.advice: 玄 is conventionally rendered 'mystère' but 同謂之玄 means 'both are called the profound/mystery'; ensure consistency and note 玄之又玄 = 'mystery upon mystery'.

payload.translation: 道は言及すべきではない。名は言及すべきではない。無名は天地の始まり、有名は万物の母である。常無を欲せず、その妙を見極める。常欲を有して、その境界を見極める。この二つは同一の源から出ているが、異なる名称を持つ。これを玄と呼び、玄之又玄。衆妙の門である。

issues.span: 道は言及すべきではない。名は言及すべきではない。
issues.advice: The source says 道可道非常道 / 名可名非常名 — 'the Dao that can be spoken is not the constant Dao; the name that can be named is not the constant name.' The translation drops 非常道/非常名 and turns it into a prohibition ('should not be mentioned'), which is a serious mistranslation.

issues.span: 常無を欲せず、その妙を見極める。常欲を有して、その境界を見極める。
issues.advice: Source is 常無欲以觀其妙 / 常有欲以觀其徼 — 'constantly without desire, to observe its wonder; constantly with desire, to observe its boundaries.' The translation negates 常無欲 ('does not desire the constant non-being'), inverting the meaning.

issues.span: 無名は天地の始まり、有名は万物の母である。
issues.advice: Source 無名天地之始 有名萬物之母 — 'the nameless is the beginning of heaven and earth; the named is the mother of all things.' Meaning is roughly preserved, but 無名/有名 should be rendered as 'the nameless'/'the named' rather than treated as bare nouns; acceptable but could be clearer.

issues.span: 玄之又玄
issues.advice: Rendered as a fragment '玄之又玄。' without a predicate; should convey 'mystery upon mystery' as a phrase, e.g. 玄にしてまた玄, to match the source's 同謂之玄 玄之又玄.

issues.span: これを玄と呼び、玄之又玄。衆妙の門である。
issues.advice: Source 同謂之玄 玄之又玄 衆妙之門 — 'together called the mystery; mystery upon mystery, the gate of all wonders.' The final clause 衆妙の門である lacks the connective tying it to 玄之又玄; the sense of 'gate of all wonders' should be explicit.

issues.span: 常無を欲せず
issues.advice: Unnatural Japanese construction; 常無/常欲 are not natural objects of 欲する. Rephrase to express 'without constant desire' / 'with constant desire'.

payload.translation: 道は言及すべきではない。名は言及すべきではない。無名は天地の始まり、有名は万物の母である。常無を欲せず、その妙を観ず。常欲を有して、その徼を観ず。これらは同一の源から出ているが、異なる名称を持つ。これを玄と呼び、玄之又玄。衆妙の門である。

issues.span: 道は言及すべきではない。名は言及すべきではない。
issues.advice: The source says 道可道非常道 / 名可名非常名 — 'the Dao that can be spoken is not the constant Dao; the name that can be named is not the constant name.' The translation reverses the meaning into a prohibition ('should not be mentioned') and drops 常道/常名 entirely. Render the conditional/relative sense and the notion of the constant Dao/name.

issues.span: 常無を欲せず、その妙を観ず。常欲を有して、その徼を観ず。
issues.advice: Source is 常無欲以觀其妙 / 常有欲以觀其徼 — 'constantly without desire, thereby observe its subtlety; constantly with desire, thereby observe its manifestations.' The translation negates the first clause ('常無を欲せず') and misparses 常無欲/常有欲. Restore the parallel 'without desire / with desire' structure.

issues.span: 無名は天地の始まり、有名は万物の母である。
issues.advice: Source: 無名天地之始 有名萬物之母 — 'The nameless is the beginning of heaven and earth; the named is the mother of the ten thousand things.' 無名/有名 are better rendered as 'the nameless/the named' rather than treated as bare nouns; acceptable but clarify.

issues.span: これを玄と呼び、玄之又玄。衆妙の門である。
issues.advice: Source: 同謂之玄 玄之又玄 衆妙之門 — 'Both are called the mystery; mystery upon mystery, the gate of all subtleties.' The translation breaks the final clause into a fragment and loses the appositive relation ('the gate of all subtleties'). Render 玄之又玄 as 'mystery upon mystery' and connect 衆妙之門 as a predicate of 玄.

issues.span: 徼
issues.advice: 徼 (jiào) means 'manifestation/boundary/outcome' in this context; ensure a consistent rendering distinct from 妙 (subtlety).

issues.span: 玄之又玄。衆妙の門である。
issues.advice: Sentence fragment; integrate into a coherent clause.
